scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for technical-grade phosphorus oxychloride (POCl3). It finds wide application as a catalyst and chlorinating agent in dyestuff, pesticide, and pharmaceutical industries. It is also a key intermediate in manufacturing phosphoric acid tri-esters, which are utilized in plasticizers and as additives for motor fuels and lubricating oils.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under Quality Control Orders issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, Government of India, all technical-grade Phosphorus Oxychloride manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial chemical liquids, as it is reserved strictly for gold and silver jewelry under national BIS frameworks.

requirements.detail: Every container of Phosphorus Oxychloride conforming to this standard must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) alongside the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).
The word 'Poisonous' together with the hazardous substance symbol specified in IS 1260 (Part 1) must be clearly printed on the container label.
Each container must prominently display the following warning: 'CAUTION — Phosphorus oxychloride is highly corrosive. When mixed with water, it decomposes with evolution of heat.'
The material must possess a minimum assay purity of 98 percent by mass of POCl3, determined via the acidimetric or excess silver nitrate back-titration testing procedures.

To ensure process safety and avoid downstream product contamination, trace impurities are strictly limited: Iron (as Fe) must not exceed 0.000 5 percent by mass (5 ppm), and Arsenic (as As) is capped at 0.000 2 percent by mass (2 ppm). Tests can be conducted chemically or via ICP-OES/ICP-MS.
requirements.clause_reference: Table 1 (Sl No. iv, v) & Clauses B-5, B-6, B-8

requirements.detail: Free Phosphorus Trichloride (PCl3) content is capped at a maximum of 0.3 percent by mass. It must be analyzed using Gas Chromatography with a Nitrogen Phosphorus Detector (NPD) under controlled temperature and pressure environments.

The fuming liquid must be colourless to pale yellow with an irritating odour. It must have a relative density of 1.64 to 1.67 at 27 °C, and a boiling range of 104 °C to 108 °C for 95 percent distillation by volume.
requirements.clause_reference: Clauses 3.1, Table 1 (Sl No. i, ii) & Clause B-2

requirements.detail: The highly corrosive chemical must be packed in drums fitted with polyethylene liners, in high-density polyethylene (HDPE) carboys, or in clean glass carboys.
Random container selection for testing must conform to Table 3 based on consignment lot sizes: up to 50 containers (select 3), 51-100 (4), 101-150 (5), 151-300 (7), and 301 and above (10).

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11657 : 2025 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification establishing physical, chemical, and safety quality requirements for technical-grade Phosphorus Oxychloride (POCl3). Widely used as a chlorinating agent, catalyst, and intermediate for manufacturing plasticizers, dyestuffs, pesticides, and pharmaceuticals, it is subject to strict Quality Control Orders issued by the Indian government. This second revision updates referenced standards and incorporates modern testing alternatives—specifically permitting ICP-OES and ICP-MS for evaluating trace iron (maximum 5 ppm) and arsenic (maximum 2 ppm) impurities. It enforces a high purity of at least 98% POCl3 while capping unreacted phosphorus trichloride at 0.3%. Given its corrosive properties and dangerous hazard of decomposing with intense heat when in contact with water, all containers must prominently carry standard 'Poisonous' markings and a dedicated moisture-reaction caution label.
